32: /** Thrown when a library write's `updated_at` precondition doesn't match — i.e. someone else
33:  *  saved between this request's read and its write. `status` is read by index.ts's error
34:  *  middleware, same as the shared `CampaignArchivedError` family. */
35: export class LibraryConflictError extends Error {
36:   readonly status = 409;
37:   constructor() {
38:     super('Someone else saved the library while you were editing. Reload and reapply your change.');
39:   }
40: }
41: 
42: /** Every library write is a read-modify-write of the *entire* 16-key blob, so without a
43:  *  precondition two admins editing unrelated records in unrelated collections silently clobber
44:  *  each other — last writer wins, and the changelog records both as successful. `version` is the
45:  *  row's `updated_at` exactly as Postgres returned it; hand it back to `saveLibrary` to make the
46:  *  write conditional.
47:  *
48:  *  Caveat worth knowing: this is millisecond-resolution time, not a monotonic counter, so two
49:  *  writes landing inside the same millisecond could both pass the check. Closing that properly
50:  *  needs a real version column and a migration; for a tool with a handful of admins the time
51:  *  precondition removes the realistic window, and it needs no schema change. */
52: export async function getLibraryWithVersion(): Promise<{ library: Library; version: string }> {
53:   const { data, error } = await supabaseAdmin.from('library').select('data, updated_at').eq('id', 'singleton').maybeSingle();
54:   if (error) throw error;
55:   if (!data) throw new Error('Library not seeded');
56:   const raw = data.data as Library;
57:   const version = data.updated_at as string;
58:   const normalized = normalizeLibrary(raw);
59:   // Self-heal a Library row missing a field added after it was seeded, so future reads don't
60:   // need to repeat this — same pattern as getSheet's Recoveries/Scars backfill. Compares every
61:   // key rather than the six this used to name by hand: villains/npcs/locations (0.35.0) and
62:   // loadTiers were all added later and were never in that list, so a row missing one of them
63:   // re-normalized on every single read and never healed.
64:   const healed = (Object.keys(normalized) as (keyof Library)[]).some((k) => normalized[k] !== raw[k]);
65:   if (healed) {
66:     try {
67:       return { library: normalized, version: await saveLibrary(normalized, version) };
68:     } catch (err) {
69:       // Another request healed it first. Ours is equivalent, so serve it and let the caller's
70:       // own write fail its precondition if it has one — never fail a *read* over this.
71:       if (!(err instanceof LibraryConflictError)) throw err;
72:     }
73:   }
74:   return { library: normalized, version };
75: }

1: -- ASoHaV — initial Postgres schema for Supabase.
2: --
3: -- Design notes:
4: --   * auth.users (managed by Supabase Auth) is the identity table. `profiles` carries the
5: --     app-specific fields (display name, content-admin flag) keyed to it 1:1.
6: --   * Every table has RLS enabled. This matters even for tables the app server always reads/
7: --     writes with the service-role key: Supabase auto-exposes every table over PostgREST to
8: --     the public anon key unless RLS is on, so enabling it is the default-deny switch, not an
9: --     optional hardening step.
10: --   * Only SELECT policies are defined for the `authenticated` role. All INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
11: --     stays behind the service-role key in the Express server, which is where the actual
12: --     business rules live (Bond handshake, sheet ownership, admin-only library writes) — this
13: --     migration does not try to re-express those as RLS policies. SELECT policies exist so
14: --     that (a) Supabase Realtime can correctly scope which row-change events a browser client
15: --     receives, and (b) the anon/authenticated key can't read data it shouldn't via PostgREST.
16: --   * Play-state aggregates (a character's sheet, the shared Party record, a Bond) are stored
17: --     as JSONB, matching the shape in packages/shared/src/types.ts exactly — that TypeScript
18: --     stays the wire contract. The library (game content) is one JSONB singleton row, same as
19: --     the SQLite version, so the existing admin validate()/referencedBy() logic ports untouched.
20: 
21: create extension if not exists pgcrypto;
22: 
23: -- ---------- profiles (extends auth.users) ----------
24: 
25: create table public.profiles (
26:   id uuid primary key references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
27:   name text not null,
28:   is_admin boolean not null default false,
29:   created_at timestamptz not null default now()
30: );
31: 
32: -- Auto-create a profile row on signup. `name` comes from the signUp() call's
33: -- options.data.name (Supabase stores arbitrary signup metadata on raw_user_meta_data);
34: -- falls back to the email's local part if that's missing.
35: create or replace function public.handle_new_user()
36: returns trigger
37: language plpgsql
38: security definer set search_path = public
39: as $$
40: begin
41:   insert into public.profiles (id, name)
42:   values (new.id, coalesce(new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'name', split_part(new.email, '@', 1)));
43:   return new;
44: end;
45: $$;
46: 
47: create trigger on_auth_user_created
48:   after insert on auth.users
49:   for each row execute function public.handle_new_user();

51: -- ---------- campaigns / characters / memberships / invites ----------
52: -- Tables are created before the RLS helper functions below, since those functions are
53: -- `language sql` and Postgres resolves their body against the schema at CREATE time (unlike
54: -- `plpgsql`, which only stores the text) — the functions would fail to create otherwise.

56: create table public.campaigns (
57:   id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
58:   name text not null,
59:   gm_user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id),
60:   created_at timestamptz not null default now()
61: );

63: create table public.characters (
64:   id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
65:   name text not null,
66:   player_name text not null,

68:   campaign_id uuid not null references public.campaigns (id) on delete cascade
69: );

74:   campaign_id uuid not null references public.campaigns (id) on delete cascade,
75:   role text not null check (role in ('GM', 'Player')),

78: );

82:   campaign_id uuid not null references public.campaigns (id) on delete cascade,
83:   email text not null,
84:   code text not null unique,
85:   sent_at timestamptz not null default now(),

161: -- Every table has RLS enabled — see the design note at the top of this file for why that
162: -- matters even for tables the app server always accesses via the service-role key.

188: alter table public.invites enable row level security;

-- ASoHaV — initial Postgres schema for Supabase.
--
-- Design notes:
--   * auth.users (managed by Supabase Auth) is the identity table. `profiles` carries the
--     app-specific fields (display name, content-admin flag) keyed to it 1:1.
--   * Every table has RLS enabled. This matters even for tables the app server always reads/
--     writes with the service-role key: Supabase auto-exposes every table over PostgREST to
--     the public anon key unless RLS is on, so enabling it is the default-deny switch, not an
--     optional hardening step.
--   * Only SELECT policies are defined for the `authenticated` role. All INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
--     stays behind the service-role key in the Express server, which is where the actual
--     business rules live (Bond handshake, sheet ownership, admin-only library writes) — this
--     migration does not try to re-express those as RLS policies. SELECT policies exist so
--     that (a) Supabase Realtime can correctly scope which row-change events a browser client
--     receives, and (b) the anon/authenticated key can't read data it shouldn't via PostgREST.
--   * Play-state aggregates (a character's sheet, the shared Party record, a Bond) are stored
--     as JSONB, matching the shape in packages/shared/src/types.ts exactly — that TypeScript
--     stays the wire contract. The library (game content) is one JSONB singleton row, same as
--     the SQLite version, so the existing admin validate()/referencedBy() logic ports untouched.
